result.topic_en: Euler computes the variation of the integral of Z dx when Z contains an auxiliary integral Phi, introduces V = integral of L dx vanishing at x = a, and derives the modified Euler–Lagrange equation that depends on the endpoint x = a.
result.transcription:
120 DE METHODO
Solutio.
Cum sit $\delta\int Zdx=\int\delta Zdx$, quaeramus ante omnia $\delta Z$, ac primo quidem statim patet esse
$\delta Z=L\delta\Phi+N\delta y+P\delta p+Q\delta q+R\delta r$ etc.
vbi, vt ante, habebitur
$\delta p=\frac{d\delta y}{dx}$; $\delta q=\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}$; $\delta r=\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3}$; $\delta s=\frac{d^4\delta y}{dx^4}$ etc.
verum ob $\delta\Phi=\delta\int\mathfrak{Z}dx=\int\delta\mathfrak{Z}dx$, erit simili modo
$\delta\mathfrak{Z}=\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.
hincque
$\delta\Phi=\int dx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.)
Cum igitur primum membrum formulae $\delta\int Zdx$ sit $Ldx\delta\Phi$ erit
$\int Ldx\delta\Phi=\int Ldx\int(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.$)dx$
Ponatur nunc $\int Ldx=V$, ac habebitur
$\int Ldx\delta\Phi=V\int dx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.)
$-\int Vdx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.)
Perinde hic est, qua lege integrale $\int Ldx=V$ capiatur, quamcunque enim constantem adiiceremus, ea in hac expressione iterum tolleretur. Ponamus ergo istud integrale ita capi, vt euanescat, posito $x=a$, et quia variatio differentialis ad terminum $x=a$ accommodari debet, erit
$\int Ldx\delta\Phi=-\int Vdx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r+$ etc.)
ad quod si addantur reliquae partes, colligimus fore
$\delta\int Zdx=\int dx(N-V\mathfrak{N})\delta y+(P-V\mathfrak{P})\delta p+(Q-V\mathfrak{Q})\delta q$ etc.
vbi

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 121
vbi, si reductiones supra indicatas adhibeamus, prodibit ista variatio differentialis iam ad terminum $x=a$ adstricta:
$\int\delta ydx((N-V\mathfrak{N})-\frac{d(P-V\mathfrak{P})}{dx}+\frac{dd(Q-V\mathfrak{Q})}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3(R-V\mathfrak{R})}{dx^3}+$ etc.)
$+\delta y((P-V\mathfrak{P})-\frac{d(Q-V\mathfrak{Q})}{dx}+\frac{dd(R-V\mathfrak{R})}{dx^2}-$ etc.)
$+\frac{d\delta y}{dx}((Q-V\mathfrak{Q})-\frac{d(R-V\mathfrak{R})}{dx}+$ etc.)
$+\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}((R-V\mathfrak{R})-$ etc.)
cuius expressionis constitutio per se est manifesta.
Coroll. 1.
Haec ergo solutio ex praecedente oritur, si loco quantitatum simplicium N, P, Q, R, etc. substituantur hae compositae:
$N-V\mathfrak{N}$, $P-V\mathfrak{P}$, $Q-V\mathfrak{Q}$, $R-V\mathfrak{R}$ etc.
vbi est $V=\int Ldx$, integrali hoc ita sumto, vt euanescat, posito $x=a$.
Coroll. 2.
Si igitur formula integralis $\int Zdx$ debeat reddi maximum vel minimum pro termino $x=a$, efficiendum est, vt ex variatione omnium valorum intermediorum ipsius $y$ nulla variatio differentialis resultet, vnde relatio inter $x$ et $y$ ita definitur, vt sit:
$(N-V\mathfrak{N})-\frac{d(P-V\mathfrak{P})}{dx}+\frac{dd(Q-V\mathfrak{Q})}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3(R-V\mathfrak{R})}{dx^3}+$ etc. $=0$
quae ergo relatio iam terminum praescriptum $x=a$ inuoluit, ita vt, si alius terminus praescribatur, alia quoque relatio indefinita inter $x$ et $y$ esset resultatura, propterea quod quantitas V hunc valorem $x=a$ in se complectitur.
Tom.X.Nou.Comm. Q Coroll.

items.quote: Perinde hic est, qua lege integrale $\int Ldx=V$ capiatur, quamcunque enim constantem adiiceremus, ea in hac expressione iterum tolleretur.
items.english: It makes no difference here by what rule the integral ∫L dx = V is taken, for whatever constant we add would be removed again in this expression.

items.quote: Haec ergo solutio ex praecedente oritur, si loco quantitatum simplicium N, P, Q, R, etc. substituantur hae compositae:
items.english: This solution therefore arises from the preceding one if, in place of the simple quantities N, P, Q, R etc., these composite ones are substituted: N−V𝔑, P−V𝔓, Q−V𝔔, R−V𝔑 etc., where V = ∫L dx taken so as to vanish at x = a.

items.quote: quae ergo relatio iam terminum praescriptum $x=a$ inuoluit, ita vt, si alius terminus praescribatur, alia quoque relatio indefinita inter $x$ et $y$ esset resultatura
items.english: This relation therefore already involves the prescribed endpoint x = a, so that if another endpoint were prescribed, a different indefinite relation between x and y would result, since the quantity V contains this value x = a.
